results.api: NostrClient(BasicOkHttpWebSocket.Builder).subscribe(subId, {relay: [filter]}, SubscriptionListener) (Amethyst's relay pool)
results.notes: Quartz's client delivers events unverified; Amethyst verifies in LocalCache.justVerify with Quartz's Event.verify() (id via EventHasher.hashIdCheck, then Schnorr), and the listener does the same, inline on the relay's delivery coroutine. Parser: Kite (KiteReader, Quartz's own). NostrClient is Quartz's pool, used here with one relay, as Amethyst uses it. keepConnected() opens the socket in setup, then 1 s to settle: a REQ sent while the new connection replays its filters can go out twice.

results.api: NostrClient.subscribe + Quartz's ParallelEventVerifier accessory (batched Event.verify() on Dispatchers.Default)
results.notes: As quartz-nostrclient, but the listener submits each event to ParallelEventVerifier (default batch 256, parallelism 8), which fans Event.verify() out over Dispatchers.Default and delivers in order. Quartz's documented speed option (an opt-in accessory; Amethyst still verifies inline on the per-relay coroutine, quartz-nostrclient), so it is a ranked entry of its own, like other libraries' speed options; it verifies on several cores, which the CPU columns show.

results.api: StandaloneRelayClient(url, BasicOkHttpWebSocket.Builder, RelayConnectionListener).sendRequest(subId, [filter])
results.notes: Quartz's single-relay client, without the pool: EVENT/EOSE messages (decoded by Kite) reach the listener's onIncomingMessage, which runs Event.verify() inline as quartz-nostrclient does. Same 1 s settle after connect.

results.api: NostrClient.fetchAllWithHooks({relay: [filter]}) { relay, event -> ... } (accessory; returns at EOSE)
results.notes: Quartz's fetch accessory with a per-event hook, over the same NostrClient and socket as quartz-nostrclient: the listener pushes each event into an UNLIMITED channel, one loop drains it and calls the hook in arrival order; the hook runs Event.verify() and keeps the verified events, which the accessory collects into its result list (returned at EOSE, so every event stays reachable until the run ends). No dedup. idleTimeoutMs 60 s. Run in a coroutine on the client's Dispatchers.IO scope; EOSE = the accessory returning.

results.api: NostrClient.fetchAll(relay, [filter]) (accessory; suspends until EOSE, returns List<Event>)
results.notes: fetchAll is fetchAllWithHooks with a hook that dedups by id (a HashSet of every id), then sorts the list newest-first (DefaultFeedOrderEvent). It does not verify: the app verifies each event of the returned list with Event.verify(), inside the run, after the accessory returns. The dedup runs before any verification, so a forged copy that arrives first takes the id and the genuine event is dropped as a duplicate: it fails the forged-content and forged-sig checks (98 of 197 delivered). idleTimeoutMs 60 s; same pool, socket and coroutine as quartz-fetchallwithhooks.

results.api: NostrClient.fetchAsFlow(relay, [filter]).collect { list -> ... } (accessory; completes at EOSE)
results.notes: fetchAsFlow: a callbackFlow whose listener dedups by id (a HashSet of every id), appends to an EventListAccumulator and sends a snapshot view of the whole list per event, conflated (a slow collector sees only the newest list); it completes at EOSE. The collector verifies the events appended since its previous emission with Event.verify(). The dedup runs before any verification, so a forged copy that arrives first censors the genuine event: it fails the forged-content and forged-sig checks (98 of 197 delivered). Same pool, socket and coroutine as quartz-fetchallwithhooks.

results.api: NostrClient.fetch(relay, filters) { event -> } (accessory; returns at EOSE with the count)
results.notes: Quartz's one-relay read: one REQ, every event handed to the callback unverified, in arrival order, on the relay's delivery coroutine (no flow in between; startReq registers the REQ and the callback runs as a SubscriptionListener would); nothing collected, deduped or sorted; returns at EOSE. The callback verifies with Event.verify(), as quartz-nostrclient's listener does. Same pool and socket as quartz-nostrclient, run in a coroutine on the client's Dispatchers.IO scope.

results.api: NostrClient.fetchEvents(relay, filters): Flow<Event> (accessory; completes at EOSE)
results.notes: fetch as a cold Flow of single events: a callbackFlow over startReq, each event handed over with a suspending send (default 64-slot buffer) and verified by the collector with Event.verify(); one coroutine hop per event more than quartz-fetch. Completes at EOSE.

results.api: Client.subscribe(ReqTarget.single) + Client.notifications().next() (UniFFI over JNA)
results.notes: All client work runs in Rust: id (verify_id) + signature checked by the relay task before the event is saved to the default in-memory events tracker and announced; a per-client LRU caches verified (id, sig) pairs, so every run builds a new Client. Drops expired (NIP-40) events by design. The notification channel also carries every relay message, so two notifications cross JNA per event, and the EOSE only arrives as a Message notification: the app calls asEnum() on every Message (a clone of the event plus a JNA call, per event) to spot it. ClientBuilder.notificationChannelSize(65536) (default 4096): the broadcast channel drops what a slower reader has not taken yet, and the JNA reader falls behind (with the default, `all` lost 60-65% of its events, a different number every run). alloc_bytes counts only the JVM side (JNA handles, strings); the Rust heap is not counted.

results.api: Client.streamEvents(ReqTarget.single) read with ClientEventStream.next() until it ends at EOSE
results.notes: The short-lived stream API (default exit policy ExitOnEOSE); EOSE = the stream's end. The stream is fed from the relay's own notification broadcast (2048, not settable from the bindings) through a 512-slot channel, so a reader slower than the relay loses events. Otherwise as nostr-sdk-subscribe.

results.api: NostrPool.connectRelay + pool.subscribe(NostrFilter, PassthroughEventTracker::new), setVerifyMatchLocally(false), event/EOSE listeners, sub.open()
results.crypto: Bouncy Castle 1.84 secp256k1 (pure Java, ECAlgorithms.sumOfTwoMultiplies) via nge-platform-jvm's Schnorr; JDK SHA-256
results.notes: NostrRelay verifies every EVENT (id + signature) before listeners see it (verifyEvents, default on), on the common ForkJoinPool (parallelEvents, default on). Subscribes with the library's PassthroughEventTracker (seen() is always false: no per-event dedup set; the pool's default ForwardSlidingWindowEventTracker treats every event older than ~30 min as already seen once 21 events arrived, so a history sync gets ~22 events) and setVerifyMatchLocally(false) (no local re-match of every event against the filter). The pool drops expired (NIP-40) events. Parser: Gson (nge-platform). Needs -Dnge-platforms.allowLoopbackInURIs=true for a loopback relay (set by the harness).

results.api: NostrService.request(RequestMessage, onRelayMessage) + deserializedEvent(eventJson)
results.websocket: Ktor 3.5.0 WebSockets on the OkHttp engine (OkHttp 5.5.1)
results.notes: The relay client hands over the event's raw JSON; the library's deserializedEvent parses it (kotlinx.serialization) and validates it (Event.isValid: id, then Schnorr), throwing on invalid events (and printing a line for each to stdout). Connects lazily inside request(): the connect is in the timed part. Its filter always carries "kinds":[] (no way to leave it out); the relay ignores filters. Its Tag holds 2-4 strings and deserialization throws on any other length, so valid events with a 1-element or 5+-element tag (imeta, ...) are rejected.

results.api: RelayPool.subscribe(filters, SubscriptionListener) (what NostrClient.subscribe delegates to)
results.websocket: Spring StandardWebSocketClient 6.2.10 on Tomcat JSR-356 client 10.1.44
results.crypto: pure-Java BIP-340 on BigInteger (nostr-java-core Schnorr), JDK SHA-256
results.notes: Slow pass: one timed run (no warmup for Dart, JVM and Ruby), in the same batch as the other rows. The pool never verifies and the library has no event verify; the listener checks the id with EventSerializer.serializeAndComputeId (its Jackson NIP-01 serializer) and the signature with nostr.crypto.schnorr.Schnorr.verify. Parser: Jackson. backlogTimeout set to --timeout-ms (the default 10 s announces EOSE on its own). The library logs every event at INFO (EventMessage.convertValue: log.info("Converting map to GenericEvent: {}", map)); it costs nothing here only because no SLF4J provider is on the classpath (slf4j-api's no-op logger), as in an app that configures its logger above INFO. The subscription deduplicates by the id field before the listener sees the event (RelaySubscription.deliverIfNotAlreadySeen -> DeliveredEventWindow.isFirstSighting) and nothing in the library verifies first, so a forged copy that arrives first is rejected by the listener and the genuine event that follows is dropped as already seen: it fails the forged-content and forged-sig checks (98 of 197 delivered).

Subscribes with the library's PassthroughEventTracker (seen() is always false: no per-event dedup set; the pool's default ForwardSlidingWindowEventTracker treats every event older than ~30 min as already seen once 21 events arrived, so a history sync gets ~22 events) and setVerifyMatchLocally(false) (no local re-match of every event against the filter). The pool drops expired (NIP-40) events. Parser: Gson (nge-platform). Needs -Dnge-platforms.allowLoopbackInURIs=true for a loopback relay (set by the harness).

results.api: RelayPool.subscribe(filters, SubscriptionListener) (what NostrClient.subscribe delegates to)
results.websocket: Spring StandardWebSocketClient 6.2.10 on Tomcat JSR-356 client 10.1.44
results.crypto: pure-Java BIP-340 on BigInteger (nostr-java-core Schnorr), JDK SHA-256
results.notes: The pool never verifies and the library has no event verify; the listener checks the id with EventSerializer.serializeAndComputeId (its Jackson NIP-01 serializer) and the signature with nostr.crypto.schnorr.Schnorr.verify. Parser: Jackson. backlogTimeout set to --timeout-ms (the default 10 s announces EOSE on its own). The library logs every event at INFO (EventMessage.convertValue: log.info("Converting map to GenericEvent: {}", map)); it costs nothing here only because no SLF4J provider is on the classpath (slf4j-api's no-op logger), as in an app that configures its logger above INFO. The subscription deduplicates by the id field before the listener sees the event (RelaySubscription.deliverIfNotAlreadySeen -> DeliveredEventWindow.isFirstSighting) and nothing in the library verifies first, so a forged copy that arrives first is rejected by the listener and the genuine event that follows is dropped as already seen: it fails the forged-content and forged-sig checks (98 of 197 delivered).

results.api: NostrService.request(RequestMessage, onRelayMessage) + deserializedEvent(eventJson)
results.websocket: Ktor 3.5.0 WebSockets on the OkHttp engine (OkHttp 5.5.1)
results.notes: The relay client hands over the event's raw JSON; the library's deserializedEvent parses it (kotlinx.serialization) and validates it (Event.isValid: id, then Schnorr), throwing on invalid events (and printing a line for each to stdout). Connects lazily inside request(): the connect is in the timed part. Its filter always carries "kinds":[] (no way to leave it out); the relay ignores filters. Its Tag holds 2-4 strings and deserialization throws on any other length, so valid events with a 1-element or 5+-element tag (imeta, ...) are rejected.
